answer: Gradient-release escrow pays each identity's rewards through three vesting stages—river, terrace, summit—releasing a fixed fraction only after aged peer attestations. A newcomer bonds 50 credits, pays 2 credits per quorum attempt capped at three per epoch, and waits twelve epochs for withdrawal; trust accrues from distinct, independently aged attestations. A coordinated ring fails because internal attestations do not satisfy the quorum's independence test, so its rewards stay locked while bonds age.
